thing.text:
RESORT INFINITY

Everything is out the back
door: the cottages, the desk,
the bell.

Go outside.

thing.note: The resort’s own machinery, which you never need to touch: six behaviours, one per guest, three robots each. SPACE here is the six guests arriving at once — they write to the post and walk to their cottages as soon as a clerk answers. Nothing in them knows how many guests there are.
Guest 1’s own three robots: ask the desk where to live, walk to the cottage it is given, and ask again when the bell rings. They work on guest 1, and on nothing else.

active.name: Ask for a place

team.name: Stand at my address
team.note: A number has landed on my nest: that is my address. Works out where that cottage stands along the row, remembers it as my place, and walks there.

team.name: Move when told to
team.note: A pad has landed on my nest: the bell, rung for every guest. Sends [where I live, my own bird] to the moving office and takes my place out of the box, so that the answer puts a new one in.

active.note: Leads. My number is still in the box, so I have nowhere to live: sends [my number, my own bird] to the desk and takes my number out as it goes, so I never ask twice.

thing.note: The bell: SPACE here and every guest already housed hears it, writes [where I live | bird] to the moving office, and waits to be told where to go.

active.name: Ring the bell
active.note: Rings once: gives every guest the pad "a move, please", then switches this behaviour off again through the bird on the perch.

thing.text:
RESORT INFINITY

You are the clerk. Eleven
cottages stand in a row,
numbered from the left. Guests
arrive at the gate; every
guest needs a cottage, and no
two may share one.

Each guest has robots of its
own (inside the pad "the
guests"): it asks the desk
where to live and walks to
that cottage. You never need
to touch those.

What is yours is the
arithmetic: a robot at the
desk that says WHICH cottage,
and later one that says WHERE
TO MOVE.

Set the Speed to 4x or 8x: a
resort takes a while at
walking pace.

PROBLEM 1
The first infinite group

Six guests wait at the gate,
numbered 1 to 6, and more are
behind them for ever.

The box on the grass with a
nest in it is the DESK. Point
at the pad "the guests", hand
empty, and press SPACE: every
guest writes to that nest, the
post, and waits.

A clerk answers each letter
with a cottage number: train
one (see HOW TO TRAIN THE
CLERK), or drop the desk on
the clerk already trained, by
the fence. The drop sets it to
work: do not press Start. Each
guest walks to its cottage.

Which cottage should guest 1
have?

HOW TO TRAIN THE CLERK

SPACE on "the guests" first,
so that letters lie on the
post. Take a little robot from
its stack, set it on the
grass, and drop the desk ON
it: its thought bubble opens
and you are teaching it.

Take the [number | bird]
letter off the post onto a
spot; copy the number; give
the copy to the bird; Dusty
takes the empty letter. Ruby
erases the number in its
thought: any number will do.

Leave the bubble and press
Start. With the post empty the
clerk dozes, which is what a
clerk does.

PROBLEM 2
Five more, and no room

Five more guests arrive and
every cottage is taken. Nobody
is turned away: everybody
housed moves FIVE along, and
the newcomers take 1 to 5.

The glass house by the desk is
the MOVING OFFICE. SPACE on
"ring the bell": every housed
guest writes to its post,
[where I live | bird], and
waits to be told where to go.
A robot of yours in the office
answers (see HOW TO TRAIN THE
MOVER).

When cottages 1 to 5 stand
empty, SPACE on "five more
guests".

Why does this work here, and
not in a hundred-room hotel?

HOW TO TRAIN THE MOVER

Ring the bell first, so that
letters lie on the office
post. Take a little robot from
its stack and drop it ON the
moving office: it steps
inside. Click the door to go
in, and the lesson begins.

Take the letter off the post
onto a spot. Drop a fresh
number, 5 with a +, on its
number. Give the number to the
bird. Dusty takes the empty
letter. Ruby erases the number
in its thought: any number
will do. Then leave: it works
inside, and the guests move.

THE ROW GOES ON

Eleven cottages stand in a
row, counted from the left,
and a guest given a number
walks to that cottage.

The row does not stop at the
fence: guest 12 would walk
past it, and guest a thousand
a long way past.

Nothing in these robots knows
how many guests there are.
That is the whole of it.

thing.name: Next address
thing.note: Problem 1, answered: guest i lives at cottage i. Takes the [number, bird] letter off the post and gives the bird a copy of the number.

thing.name: Move up five
thing.note: Problem 2, answered: everybody moves up five, which empties cottages 1 to 5 for the newcomers. In the moving office: takes the [where I live, bird] letter off the office post, adds 5, and gives the answer to the bird.
